subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <cstdint> header. SHIPPED 2026-08-25; REACHES C++98 since the face's 2026.10.02 revision, which stopped including <cstdint> (a C++11 header) and takes every name from dstdint.h, re_std's own <stdint.h> (inc/re_std/c/cstdint/dstdint.h, covered by the C workbook). cstdint.hpp re-exports each name from the global namespace with a using-declaration, so re_std::int64_t is std::int64_t from C++11 and the platform's int64_t below -- identity preserved on both of dstdint.h's backends, the platform's headers or its own definitions from the compiler's predefined macros. Every family is gated on its own limit macro, the standard's own test: the optional exact-width and pointer-sized pairs, and the mandatory least, fast and greatest-width ones too, because dstdint.h leaves out a family the build cannot spell -- the 64-bit types under ISO strict C++98 where the ABI makes them `long long`, the fast types where it cannot tell which the platform chose. Measured with gcc 13: every family present from ISO strict C++98 to C++2b on x86_64 Linux, on both backends, and the same type as std:: from C++11; on 32-bit x86 (freestanding) ISO strict C++98 has no int64_t, int_least64_t or intmax_t, as designed, and gnu++98 has all three. Granularity is a documented exception (one header, not thirty-two): every typedef has the identical dependency, so per-symbol headers would narrow nothing.
legend_blurb: <cstdint> provides the fixed-width integer typedefs (exact, least, fast, max and pointer-sized) and their limit and literal macros.

symbols.name: int8_t / uint8_t
symbols.notes: OPTIONAL in the standard -- intN_t / uintN_t exist only where the implementation has a type of exactly N bits with no padding. The standard guarantees INTN_MAX is defined if and only if the typedef is, which gives an exact preprocessor test, so the pair is gated on its own macro rather than on a compiler whitelist. Absent on a target without them -- the header still compiles. Taken from dstdint.h at every level, so the pair reaches C++98 although <cstdint> is C++11.

symbols.notes: OPTIONAL in the standard -- intN_t / uintN_t exist only where the implementation has a type of exactly N bits with no padding. symbols.notes: OPTIONAL in the standard -- intN_t / uintN_t exist only where the implementation has a type of exactly N bits with no padding. The standard guarantees INTN_MAX is defined if and only if the typedef is, which gives an exact preprocessor test, so the pair is gated on its own macro rather than on a compiler whitelist. symbols.name: int64_t / uint64_t
symbols.notes: OPTIONAL in the standard, gated on INT64_MAX like the other exact-width pairs. Several ABIs spell it `long long` -- LLP64 Windows, every 32-bit target, and macOS although `long` is 64 bits there -- and ISO strict C++98 has no `long long`, so a strict C++98 build on those targets has no int64_t: measured absent on 32-bit x86, present on x86_64 Linux (where it is `long`), and present everywhere under gnu++98. No other 64-bit type stands in, since that would break identity. Test RE_STD_HAS_INT64 where the answer must not change later in the unit: another system header can bring INT64_MAX in after this one.

symbols.name: int_leastN_t / uint_leastN_t (N=8,16,32,64)
symbols.notes: Mandatory in the standard, but gated pair by pair on INT_LEASTN_MAX: dstdint.h leaves int_least64_t / uint_least64_t out where the build cannot spell their type (ISO strict C++98 on a `long long` ABI; measured absent on 32-bit x86). The 8-, 16- and 32-bit pairs are present at every level. Smallest type with at least N bits. These are what <chrono>'s duration typedefs use, in preference to the exact-width names, so the typedefs still exist on a target that has no exact-width types.

symbols.name: int_fastN_t / uint_fastN_t (N=8,16,32,64)
symbols.notes: Mandatory in the standard, but gated pair by pair on INT_FASTN_MAX. No ABI fixes these types, and a compiler's predefined macros can disagree with the C library (Clang predefines `short` for int_fast16_t on Linux, where glibc declares `long`), so dstdint.h's own definitions provide the family only where they know which <stdint.h> the platform uses, and leave it out as a whole elsewhere. Fastest type with at least N bits; the definition of 'fastest' is the implementation's.

symbols.name: intmax_t / uintmax_t
symbols.notes: Mandatory in the standard, but gated on INTMAX_MAX: dstdint.h leaves the pair out where the platform's is a `long long` the build cannot use -- ISO strict C++98 on a `long long` ABI (measured absent on 32-bit x86) -- rather than name a narrower type and break every interface that takes intmax_t. The widest integers the implementation supports. re_std::ratio's non-type parameters are intmax_t, so this pair fixes the range of every ratio and therefore of every chrono duration period.

symbols.name: intptr_t / uintptr_t
symbols.notes: OPTIONAL -- a target need not have an integer wide enough to round-trip a void*. Gated on INTPTR_MAX, the standard's own test. dstdint.h's own definitions give it the width of an object pointer (RE_STD_POINTER_BITS) and leave it out where nothing states that width.

symbols.name: INT*_MIN / INT*_MAX / SIZE_MAX / PTRDIFF_* / WCHAR_* / WINT_* / SIG_ATOMIC_*
symbols.notes: Macros have no namespace, so there is no re_std:: spelling and none is invented. re_std's contribution is availability at every level: dstdint.h defines each one the platform did not, and asks an older C++ library that withholds them from C++ (__STDC_LIMIT_MACROS / __STDC_CONSTANT_MACROS) before including it, withdrawing the request afterwards. Every gap-fill is #ifndef-guarded -- a platform that answered is never overridden. On a compiler with neither the headers nor predefined macros, dstdint.h derives the types from <limits.h> and leaves SIZE_MAX, PTRDIFF_*, SIG_ATOMIC_*, WCHAR_* and WINT_* undefined, since nothing states their values. Prefer re_std::numeric_limits<T>, which is typed, namespaced and constexpr from C++11. The macros remain the right tool inside #if conditionals, where no function can be called -- re_std::ratio's zetta/yotta typedefs are gated on INTMAX_MAX for exactly that reason.

symbols.name: INT*_C / UINT*_C
symbols.notes: Macros have no namespace, so there is no re_std:: spelling and none is invented. re_std's contribution is availability at every level: dstdint.h defines each one the platform did not, and asks an older C++ library that withholds them from C++ (__STDC_LIMIT_MACROS / __STDC_CONSTANT_MACROS) before including it, withdrawing the request afterwards. Every gap-fill is #ifndef-guarded -- a platform that answered is never overridden. Each takes its suffix from the spelling of the type itself, not from the platform's limit macros. Clang 20 and older, freestanding, on the platform backend, give UINT8_C and UINT16_C the wrong type (WG14 DR 209, fixed in Clang 21); the own backend is the way out. Literal-suffix constructors; no numeric_limits equivalent exists, so these have no better alternative.
